name: Gamma-linolenic acid
short: In eczema trials, evening primrose and borage oil had the same mild, mainly gastrointestinal effects as placebo. One study found evening primrose oil may increase bleeding in people on warfarin.
text: Most safety evidence comes from evening primrose oil and borage oil, which are taken for their gamma-linolenic acid content. In a Cochrane review of 27 trials (1596 participants) in eczema, both oils and their placebos had the same fairly common, mild, transient adverse effects, mainly gastrointestinal; the review noted that these short-term trials do not examine long-term use and that one study found evening primrose oil may increase bleeding in people taking warfarin. Another review listed gastrointestinal upset and headaches as minor adverse effects and stated that use of evening primrose oil during pregnancy is not supported in the literature and should be avoided. In a network meta-analysis of alpha-lipoic acid and gamma-linolenic acid trials in diabetic neuropathy, most adverse events across all studies were gastrointestinal disturbances; they were not reported separately for gamma-linolenic acid.
